# Fixture: two_modules

Two modules, `core` and `app`, for file and include facts (B-08), function
facts (B-09) and module dependencies (B-11). Three translation units, all of
which parse (FR-001 criterion 1). Compiled with
`-I<fixture root>`, so `"core/core.h"` resolves from both modules.

| File | Includes |
|---|---|
| `core/core.h` | `<stddef.h>` (external: Clang's resource directory) |
| `core/core.c` | `"core.h"` (same directory), `<string.h>` (external) |
| `app/app.h` | `"core/core.h"` |
| `app/main.c` | `"app.h"`, `<stdio.h>` (external) |
| `app/legacy.c` | `"app.h"` |

`app/app.h` and `core/core.h` are reached from several TUs; each of their
include directives must be recorded once. The compilation database is
generated by the test with absolute paths. An unresolved include has its
own fixture, `unresolved_include`.

Functions (B-09): `core_length` (declared `core/core.h` 6, defined
`core/core.c` 5–7), `app_run` (declared `app/app.h` 6, defined `app/main.c`
5–7), `main` (`app/main.c` 9–11) and `legacy_run` (`app/legacy.c` 3–5).
`printf` and `strlen` are declared outside the root and are not recorded.
